transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
Most nights I end up eating until I feel uncomfortably full, even though I keep telling myself to stop earlier. It's been happening a lot lately and I'm just really struggling to get a handle on it.
After these episodes of overeating, do you ever do things to try to prevent weight gain, such as making yourself throw up, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?
No, I don't do any of those things to try to prevent weight gain. Usually, I just end up crashing on the couch because I feel so sluggish and bloated afterward.
How many times a week do these overeating episodes usually happen, and for how many months has this been going on?

This has been happening at least a couple of nights every week. It's been going on for about four months now, pretty much starting right around the time my wife took on her evening classes and extra shifts.
How do you feel emotionally after these overeating episodes? For example, do you experience intense guilt, disgust with yourself, or feel very distressed about your eating?

I mostly feel really disappointed in myself and a heavy sense of shame, thinking "you did it again" once I finally stop. I'm embarrassed enough by it that I've started hiding the eating from my wife so she doesn't see how much I'm putting away. It's more of a deep regret and physical discomfort than intense self-disgust, but it definitely weighs on me.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms align with Binge Eating Disorder, characterized by recurrent episodes of eating until uncomfortably full, loss of control, hiding eating due to embarrassment, and subsequent feelings of shame and regret, without compensatory behaviors. These episodes occur at least twice a week for four months. In ICD-10, Binge Eating Disorder is classified under F50.8 ('Other eating disorders'). F50.9 is removed as we have enough specific criteria to rule out an unspecified eating disorder.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's clinical presentation is highly characteristic of Binge Eating Disorder, which is classified under F50.8 (Other eating disorders) in ICD-10. He experiences recurrent episodes of eating large amounts of food with a sense of lack of control (unable to stop), eating until uncomfortably full, and hiding his eating from his wife due to embarrassment. These episodes are accompanied by feelings of shame, disappointment, and regret. The episodes occur at least twice a week and have been present for four months. He does not engage in any inappropriate compensatory behaviors (such as purging, laxative use, or fasting), ruling out Bulimia Nervosa.
